name: Granqvist 2005 replication: right Thomas, then bilateral burst-firing
origin: Granqvist, Fredrikson, Unge, Hagenfeldt, Valind, Larhammar & Larsson 2005 (Swedish independent replication), with equipment and software (Complex v1.15) supplied by Stan Koren
summary: A copy, for blinded self-tests, of the only fully specified independent double-blind test of the God Helmet: 15 min of the Thomas pattern over the right temporal lobe, then 15 min of burst-firing over both temporal lobes. With 89 participants (43 field, 46 unpowered helmet), Granqvist et al. found no effect of the field; absorption, temporal-lobe signs and a "new age" orientation predicted sensed presence and mystical experiences.
notes: Order and sides follow the replication record: the Thomas pattern over the right hemisphere, then burst-firing over both, 15 min each (Persinger's emails: "the 15 min of Thomas and 15 min of Burst"). Granqvist's letter: Complex v1.15 calibrated per its manual, total cycles set to 9000 "as instructed" (what the software counts as a cycle is not published), the program stopped with ctrl-alt-del after 15 min timed by a digital watch. Nature reports the fields "aimed just above and in front of the ears"; two coils per side at FT7, T7 and FT8, T8 is an inference (by Persinger's records Koren sent a 4-channel DAC010-V unit with right and left solenoids; the coil count per side is not published). Phase 1 drives only the right pair, phase 2 all four, all with the same polarity. Thomas: the exact 849-point patent table at 3 ms with 3 ms between passes (2.55 s per cycle, the Laurentian file as Buckner 2015 and Murugan 2013 describe it); that Koren's file was this table is an assumption. Burst-firing: the point values are unpublished, so the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) on 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s; lab theses give 230, 248 or 289 points) once every 4 s stands in; the paper gives no interval, and 4 s follows Martin et al. 2004 (other lab studies used 3 s). The original field was 3-7 uT; 5 uT is this helmet's maximum. Persinger and Koren blamed the null result on (1) point timing distorted by an uncalibrated fast Windows computer, (2) 15 min instead of their 20-40 min per pattern, and (3) a small box without a blindfold; Granqvist replied that blindfolds were used and the room was about 2 m2. This firmware times every point on a fixed 0.5-ms clock, so objection 1 does not apply to this copy; the 15 + 15 min are kept to copy the test. By Persinger & Koren's own account, field and sham groups both scored M = 0.3, SD = 0.5 on sensed presence, their usual sham level; Gendle & McGrath 2012 also found no field effect. No medical claim; not for people with epilepsy; stop on fear or distress. The evidence rating refers to this independent test and its null result, not to a God Helmet effect.
setting: Blindfolded, seated in a small, quiet, dim room (the "sensory deprivation context" of Granqvist & Larsson 2006). A helper who does not know the condition gives the instructions and the questionnaire; the person who starts the session uses the app's Blind option, or assigns active or sham, and says nothing. Afterwards, before unblinding, rate a 20-item exit list of unusual sensations (felt a presence, tingling, dizzy or odd, ...) 0 = never, 1 = once, 2 = frequently.
schedule: One session per person in the original (between groups). For a self-test, several Blind sessions at least a day apart, ratings recorded before the condition is revealed; fill in absorption and temporal-lobe-sign questionnaires on another day, well before (Persinger's lab gave its Personal Philosophy Inventory two to four months before exposure).
